source_citation: Diggs, Lipscomb & O'Kennon (1999), Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
evidence_scope: Factual structured summary of printed species treatment and diagnostic key, not independently verified
cautions: Historical name concepts need separate modern taxonomic corroboration before scoring

Flora explicitly discusses alternative species rank Astragalus pleianthus (Shinners) Isely; taxonomy unresolved without current accepted-name check
Flora p.634 places var. pleianthus on key branch with triangular to narrowly deltoid keel tips, at least some unnotched leaflets, racemes usually 4–10 flowers.
Historical flora says other authors elevate this variety to Astragalus pleianthus; modern rank must be reconciled.

morphology_source_reported.growth_habit: Annual as treated within A. nuttallianus species complex

morphology_source_reported.diagnostic_characters: At least some upper leaflets obtuse to subacute; keel triangular to narrowly deltoid at apex; comparatively larger flowers and more-flowered racemes than var. austrinus/trichocarpus

habitat_source_reported: Calcareous soils; prairies and open woodlands
